topic: Mark Mastrov Named to 2027 HFA Hall of Fame

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Mark Mastrov Named to 2027 HFA Hall of Fame

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The 24 Hour Fitness founder will be honored March 10 during the HFA Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Mark Mastrov is being inducted into the 2027 HFA Hall of Fame for his lasting impact on the fitness industry through entrepreneurship, innovation, and mentorship. Mark Mastrov turned a single California gym into one of the world’s most recognized fitness brands, then spent the decades that followed building businesses, mentoring leaders, and investing in the future of the fitness industry. That impact will be recognized March 10 when the 24 Hour Fitness founder is inducted into the HFA Hall of Fame during The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Mastrov built 24 Hour Fitness into a global fitness company, then launched, invested in, and supported businesses across fitness, sports, and wellness. More than 40 years after founding the company, he recently returned as an owner of 24 Hour Fitness, beginning a new chapter with the brand that helped define his career. “Mark’s influence on our industry extends far beyond the businesses he has built,” said HFA Interim President and CEO Greta Wagner. “He has consistently pushed the industry forward while creating opportunities for others to lead, grow, and succeed.

topic: Why BODY20 Is Betting on Strength Training for Women

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Why BODY20 Is Betting on Strength Training for Women

facts.label: Article
facts.value: As women put greater focus on muscle, longevity and strength, BODY20 is positioning its 20-minute EMS model as an accessible way to make resistance training part of the routine. For many women, fitness priorities are shifting from losing weight to building and maintaining strength and muscle. Roughly two-thirds of the fitness brand’s members are women, most between 35 and 55 or older. Sydney Maddox, director of fitness at BODY20, says their priorities are evolving. “The language has changed,” Maddox said. “Fewer women come in talking about getting smaller or burning calories, and more come in talking about staying strong, protecting their joints, keeping their bone health in mind, and being capable for the long run.” Maintaining muscle becomes more important with age, particularly through perimenopause and menopause. The growth of GLP-1 use has added another reason to pay attention to muscle preservation during weight loss. For BODY20, those trends point to a growing need for strength training that women can realistically incorporate into their routines. “Muscle is increasingly understood as something to build and protect rather than avoid,” Maddox said. BODY20 uses whole-body electrical muscle stimulation, or EMS, to create a strength-training stimulus in 20-minute coached sessions. Members wear a suit equipped with electrodes positioned over major muscle groups.

en.headline: Why BODY20 Is Betting on Strength Training for Women
